purpose: The US-020 AC5 class register (internal/ac5class) states, per seeded class variant, which normalized DIFFERENTIAL observation fields the variant moves. `ac5ctl run` measures those fields by comparing the pristine port arm against the mutated port arm, not against Java, so the gate stays runnable without the pinned JVM. This record is what makes that substitution exact rather than convenient: it is a real run of the pinned Java-WebSocket 1.6.0 oracle over the same request streams, showing the pristine port and live Java agree on every behavioural field. A field therefore moves against Java exactly when it moves against the pristine port.

field-by-field over the java-websocket-handshake-oracle protocol (case_id keyed; diffregressctl is request_id keyed and cannot read this tier)
measured_parity.note: recorded because the Java-quirk-emulation seed ac5-jq-handshake-unbounded-head lives on the handshake path. The exam does not reach the configured budget on any of its 49 cases — the ledger's own record 45 says the live-exam input fits the budget — so the exam cannot detect that seed either. That is why the seed carries a collision record naming its blind judges instead of a discriminating field set.

what_this_does_not_claim: It is one run of one port build against one Java build, on one host. It is not a proof that the two agree in general.
error.detail wording differs on 43 of the 97 cases and always has; internal/diffregress classifies that as identical_except_error_detail by documented design, not as parity.

The handshake tier's 49 cases were compared by an ad-hoc field walk, not by the committed comparator, because that protocol has no request_id. The number is reported for context, not as gate evidence.
